newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex adds new Bufete-built natgas plants.
newsitem.headline: Pemex adds new Bufete-built natgas plants.

text.p: Mexican state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) inaugurated on Saturday two natural gas processing plants, as part of efforts to boost output of the fuel.

Pemex's natural gas director Marcos Ramirez Silva toured the southern Tabasco state plants, one a condensates sweetener with a 24,000 barrel per day (bpd) capacity and the other a hydrocarbon processor with capacity of up to 104,000 bpd.
Bufete Industrial built the plants at a total cost of $54.3 million, Ramirez told reporters. Pemex workers told Reuters the plants were ready to begin operations.
Pemex has said these and other new natural gas plants will help process an expected rise in production in the southern Campeche Sound region.
He said Bufete would also build later this year a cryogenic plant in Reynosa, Tamaulipas state, a key natural gas export site to the United States.
The new plants help recover lost production from the fatal Cactus natural gas complex explosion a year ago, that halted production there and required Mexico to import more natural gas for months.
With the new plants, Pemex will boost its natural gas production by nine percent from its levels before the Cactus complex explosion, Ramrez said.
